company: Incitec Pivot Limited (now Dyno Nobel Limited)
title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: All Directors of the Company and Group employees collectively. Subject to the insider trading rules, the Front Page Test, the prohibition on dealing in other companies' securities on inside information and the blackout periods, but not to the standing approval requirement, the margin lending ban, the short-term and speculative dealing ban or the hedging restrictions.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Directors, other key management personnel of the Company and direct reports to the CEO (Senior Executives), and other persons who regularly possess inside information and have been advised by the Company Secretary that they are subject to special restrictions (Nominated Employees). Subject to all the additional restrictions in section 5: prior approval for every dealing, the margin lending prohibition, the short-term and speculative dealing ban, the hedging restrictions and responsibility for Connected Persons.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of the Company, including the CEO. Restricted Persons whose dealings are approved by the Chairman of the Board (the Chairman of the Audit & Risk Management Committee approves the Chairman's own dealings), and who must promptly confirm every trade to the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Senior Executives
tiers.description: Other key management personnel of the Company and direct reports to the CEO. Restricted Persons; their dealings are approved by the Company Secretary, except that the Company Secretary's own dealings are approved by the CEO.

tiers.name: Nominated Employees
tiers.description: Other persons who regularly possess inside information and who have been advised by the Company Secretary that they are subject to special restrictions under the Policy. Restricted Persons; their dealings are approved by the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: A family member who may be expected to influence, or be influenced by, the Restricted Person in dealings with Company securities (spouse, partner, children, partner's children, dependants), and any company or entity the Restricted Person is able to control. Restricted Persons must take appropriate steps to ensure they only deal where the Restricted Person could, including by obtaining clearance for their dealings.

definitions.hedging_definition: Hedging includes entering into any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding the Company's securities.

windows.start_anchor: close of trading on the ASX on 30 September each year
windows.end_anchor: the day after the announcement to ASX of the full year results

windows.start_anchor: close of trading on the ASX on 31 March each year
windows.end_anchor: the day after the announcement to ASX of the half-year results

windows.start_anchor: release of the Company's full-year or half-year results

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may specify any other blackout period from time to time (s4.4). The Company may also notify Employees that they must not deal in securities, either for a specified period or until further notice (s4.1). The Policy does not state whether these notices are confidential, but a refusal or revocation of approval must be kept confidential (s6(c)).

rules.detail: Derivatives are not named or defined. A purchased put and written call over vested, unrestricted Company securities is an arrangement that operates to limit economic risk and so is hedging; the Policy prohibits hedging only of unvested plan securities and securities under a holding lock, so hedging vested holdings is permitted, subject to prior written approval under section 5.1 (valid 5 business days), the blackout periods and the Front Page Test. No venue limitation.
rules.evidence: Hedging includes entering into any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Any derivative that limits the economic risk of unvested plan securities is prohibited absolutely; the word 'never' leaves no approval or exceptional circumstances route.
rules.evidence: Company securities acquired by a Restricted Person under an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by the Company must never be hedged prior to vesting.

rules.detail: Securities that have vested but remain subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under a plan may never be hedged, so vested shares still inside a plan holding lock cannot form part of the collared parcel.
rules.evidence: Company securities held by a Restricted Person must never be hedged while they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by the Company.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on hedging plan securities before vesting.
rules.evidence: Company securities acquired by a Restricted Person under an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by the Company must never be hedged prior to vesting.

rules.detail: Absolute ban while the securities are subject to a holding lock or a restriction on dealing under the terms of a Company equity plan.
rules.evidence: Company securities held by a Restricted Person must never be hedged while they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by the Company.

rules.detail: Section 5.4 defines hedging and then prohibits it only in the two stated cases, so hedging vested and unrestricted holdings is permitted. It is a dealing requiring prior approval on the Clearance to Trade Request Form, which may be refused without reasons, made subject to conditions or revoked at any time, must be executed within 5 business days, must fall outside the blackouts and must satisfy the Front Page Test.
rules.evidence: During any period that is not a trading blackout period under section 4.4, Restricted Persons must, prior to any proposed dealing, seek approval for the proposed dealing in the Company's securities.

rules.detail: The hedging restrictions sit in section 5 (Additional restrictions applying to Restricted Persons) and do not apply to Employees who are not Restricted Persons; for them only the insider trading prohibition, the Front Page Test and the blackout periods apply.

Monetisation is not named. A collar with a loan, prepaid forward or similar structure limits the economic risk of holding Company securities and so is hedging: permitted over vested unrestricted holdings with approval, prohibited over unvested or holding-locked plan securities. Forward contracts are expressly given as an example of a short-term dealing, so a short-dated monetisation risks breaching section 5.3, and the substance over form principle in section 1 means labels will not control the analysis.
rules.evidence: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 90 day period, and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts).

rules.detail: Short selling is expressly named as a form of prohibited speculative dealing, with no approval route. This does not on its face catch a covered hedge over shares actually held, but any naked short leg of a structure would be prohibited.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not deal in the Company's securities on a speculative basis, including short selling.

rules.detail: Securities lending by a holder is not mentioned; borrowing appears only in the description of short selling in section 5.3. A lend and return would arguably fall within the excluded dealing for dealings with no effective change to the beneficial interest.

CFDs are not named. A CFD over Company securities that limits the economic risk of a holding is hedging and so is permitted over vested unrestricted holdings with approval and prohibited over unvested or holding-locked plan securities; in practice a CFD position would usually be caught by the ban on speculative or short-term dealing.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not deal in the Company's securities on a short-term trading basis.

rules.detail: Flat prohibition with no approval, hardship or exceptional circumstances route and no security-state or tier carve-out within Restricted Persons. Given the substance over form principle, a loan secured on Company shares with margin call or LVR mechanics is likely to be treated as a margin lending arrangement in relation to the Company's securities.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons are not permitted to enter into margin lending arrangements in relation to the Company's securities.

rules.detail: The margin lending prohibition sits under 'Additional restrictions applying to Restricted Persons' and is expressed to bind Restricted Persons only; the Policy says nothing about margin lending by other Employees.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons are not permitted to enter into margin lending arrangements in relation to the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Granting a mortgage, charge, pledge or other security interest over Company securities is not mentioned and is not brought within the description of dealing in section 3, which covers buying, selling, agreeing to buy or sell, exercising options and applying for, acquiring or disposing of securities. The only recognition of a security interest is the excluded dealing for a secured lender's enforcement sale.

The only financing arrangement expressly regulated is a margin lending arrangement, which is prohibited. Secured financing generally is not addressed: there is no approval, notification or disclosure requirement for a loan secured on Company securities, and section 7(g) contemplates that secured lending may exist by excluding a secured lender's enforcement sale from the blackout and approval rules. Whether a bank facility secured on collared shares is caught depends on whether it is characterised as a margin lending arrangement, which the substance over form principle makes likely where it has margin call features.
rules.evidence: a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights.

rules.detail: Buying and selling on market within a 90 day period is prohibited, as is entering into other short term dealings, with forward contracts given as the example. Selling shares received on vesting of entitlements under an employee, executive or director equity plan within 90 days of the vesting date is expressly not a short-term dealing.
rules.evidence: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 90 day period, and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts).

clearance.approver: Chairman of the Board; for the Chairman of the Board, the Chairman of the Audit & Risk Management Committee. Requests go to the Company Secretary, who approves or forwards them.
clearance.post_trade_deadline: promptly, ideally by close of business on the day the trade is entered into
clearance.evidence: Following receipt of approval to deal, the approved dealing must occur within 5 business days following approval (or such other time specified in the approval), otherwise the approval is no longer effective and fresh approval must be sought.

clearance.approver: Company Secretary; the CEO approves the Company Secretary's own dealings. Requests are made on the Clearance to Trade Request Form in Schedule 1.
clearance.evidence: The approver is not obliged to provide reasons for any aspect of their decision, and may revoke their approval at any time. If a request is not approved or an approval is revoked, that fact must be kept confidential.

In order to request approval to deal under sections 4.5 or 5.1, you must complete a "Clearance to Trade Request Form" (in Schedule 1) and submit it to the Company Secretary, who will approve it or forward it for approval

clearance.approver: Chairman of the Board for Directors including the CEO, Chairman of the Audit & Risk Management Committee for the Chairman, CEO for the Company Secretary, and Company Secretary for all other Employees
clearance.evidence: During any period that is not a trading blackout period under section 4.4, Restricted Persons must, prior to any proposed dealing, seek approval for the proposed dealing in the Company's securities.

clearance.approver: Company Secretary, but only for a request to deal during a blackout period in exceptional circumstances under section 4.5; no standing approval requirement otherwise
clearance.evidence: If an Employee needs to deal in securities during a blackout period due to exceptional circumstances and is not in possession of any Inside Information, then, they may apply for approval to deal following the process in section 6.

short_term.basis: buying and selling securities on market within a 90 day period, plus other short term dealings such as forward contracts
carve_outs: Selling shares received on vesting of entitlements under an employee, executive or director equity plan within 90 days of the vesting date
short_term.evidence: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 90 day period, and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts). Selling shares received on vesting of entitlements under an employee, executive or director equity plan within 90 days of the vesting date is not a short-term dealing.

exceptions.approver: Chairman of the Board, Chairman of the Audit & Risk Management Committee, CEO or Company Secretary per the section 6 table
exceptions.evidence: Exceptional circumstances are likely to include severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order.

exceptions.approver: Chairman of the Board, Chairman of the Audit & Risk Management Committee, CEO or Company Secretary per the section 6 table
exceptions.evidence: Approval to deal will only be granted if the Employee's application is accompanied by sufficient evidence (in the opinion of the person providing clearance) that the dealing is the most reasonable course of action available in the circumstances.

However, where securities in the Company granted under an employee, executive or director equity plan cease to be held under the terms of that plan, any dealings in those securities must only occur in accordance with this Policy;

an investment in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in the Company's securities) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party;

financing_disclosure: Directors; following any trade in Company securities; to the Company Secretary; promptly, ideally by close of business on the day the trade is entered into (s5.5)

external_documents: Employee, executive and director equity plans operated by the Company
Clearance to Trade Request Form (Schedule 1, included in the Policy)
exemption_authority: Section 4.5: an Employee who needs to deal during a blackout period because of exceptional circumstances, likely severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order, and who holds no Inside Information, may apply for approval through the section 6 process; approval is granted only on sufficient evidence, in the clearer's opinion, that the dealing is the most reasonable course of action available. Approval will never be granted where the dealing fails the Front Page Test (s4.2). There is no power to exempt anyone from the margin lending prohibition or the hedging prohibitions in section 5.4.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons are not permitted to enter into margin lending arrangements in relation to the Company's securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg is the problem: if the facility secured on the collared shares is characterised as a margin lending arrangement it is flatly prohibited for Directors, Senior Executives and Nominated Employees, with no approval route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A facility documented as a term loan rather than a margin loan will still be assessed on its substance, so LVR tests, top-up rights and enforcement over the shares make the section 5.2 ban likely to bite.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 90 day period, and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A short-dated collar or forward leg can itself be a prohibited short-term dealing, so tenor should comfortably exceed 90 days and early termination rights should be limited.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Company securities held by a Restricted Person must never be hedged while they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of an employee, executive or director equity plan.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Vesting alone is not enough: shares still under a plan holding lock cannot be collared, so the bank must diligence lock status as well as vesting.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Sections 4.3, 4.4 and 5.1 of this Policy do not apply to ... a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If a compliant secured facility could be put in place, enforcement sales sit outside the blackout and approval rules, though this carve-out cannot cure the margin lending prohibition itself.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even an otherwise compliant collar over vested shares can be refused on perception grounds alone, and the approver need not give reasons.

bespoke_clauses.clause: During any period that is not a trading blackout period under section 4.4, Restricted Persons must, prior to any proposed dealing, seek approval for the proposed dealing in the Company's securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no free trading window: entry, roll, partial unwind and physical settlement each need fresh written approval, valid only 5 business days.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The approver is not obliged to provide reasons for any aspect of their decision, and may revoke their approval at any time. If a request is not approved or an approval is revoked, that fact must be kept confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval can be withdrawn after pricing is agreed and the client cannot explain why, so the documentation must tolerate silent withdrawal before settlement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees must not deal in Company securities: from the close of trading on the ASX on 30 September each year until the day after the announcement to ASX of the full year results ... from the close of trading on the ASX on 31 March each year until the day after the announcement to ASX of the half-year results.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The blackouts follow a 30 September financial year end, and approval is described as more likely only in the 4 weeks after each results release, so execution should be scheduled into those windows.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must take appropriate steps to ensure that their Connected Persons only deal in securities in circumstances where the Restricted Person to whom they are connected would be permitted to deal under this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the structure through a spouse, family trust or controlled entity does not escape the margin lending ban or the clearance requirement.

summary: The derivative legs of a collar are achievable for a Restricted Person, but the funding leg is the obstacle. Hedging is defined as any arrangement limiting the economic risk of holding Company securities and is prohibited only over unvested plan securities and securities under a plan holding lock, so a put and call over vested, unrestricted shares is permitted subject to prior written approval on the Clearance to Trade Request Form (Chairman for Directors, Company Secretary for Senior Executives), execution within 5 business days, the 30 September and 31 March blackouts and the Front Page Test. However, section 5.2 flatly prohibits Restricted Persons from entering into margin lending arrangements in relation to the Company's securities, with no approval route, and the express substance over form principle means a bank facility secured on the collared shares with LVR or margin call mechanics is likely to be treated as such, so a funded structure would need to be demonstrably not a margin lending arrangement. Tenor is a further constraint: forward contracts are expressly given as an example of a prohibited short term dealing and buying and selling within 90 days is banned, so the collar should run well beyond 90 days. If a compliant facility could be structured, section 7(g) helpfully excludes a secured lender's enforcement sale from the blackout and approval rules.
